body.statement: For every rational \(p\) of coefficient height \(B\), \(\mathsf{Cert}\) terminates. If \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\varnothing\), it returns the exact refinement-enumeration ledger and, for every \(G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) and every \(r\in\mathcal R_G\), a replayable real-algebraic elimination trace or rational Positivstellensatz identity proving \(\{\lambda\in\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r,a}):P_G(\lambda)=p\}=\varnothing\); these branch certificates jointly certify the empty fiber. If the fiber is nonempty, it returns for each endpoint a square-free integer isolating polynomial, a rational isolating interval, and an algebraic-weight endpoint-attaining SCM. In either branch its bit-operation count is \(R_{\Sigma}B^{O(1)}(s_{\max}D_{\max})^{O(k_{\max})}\). In the nonempty branch the endpoint algebraic degree is \(D_{\max}^{O(k_{\max})}\), and every output coefficient has bit length \(B(s_{\max}D_{\max})^{O(k_{\max})}\). The compiler derives \(R_{\Sigma},k_{\max},s_{\max},D_{\max}\) from \(d,H,L,E_{\mathcal S}^{\to},E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow}\) and the raw branch catalogues. Thus, unlike the numerical \(\varepsilon\)-sharp output of Duarte et al., the algorithm either exactly rejects an incompatible observed law branch by branch or certifies exact attained endpoints and decodes checkable SCM witnesses.
body.justification: A total certifier must distinguish observational incompatibility from a nonempty identified set and provide exact evidence in either case.
body.gap: BasuPollackRoy1996 supplies generic real-quantifier-elimination complexity and GeigerMeek1999 applies elimination to small hidden-variable models; neither derives the causal encoding size, total empty-fiber certificate ledger, endpoint witness decoder, or refinement-union certificate, while DuarteEtAl2024 stops at numerical convergence.
body.consumer: Small summary-graph analyses obtain replayable incompatibility certificates or exact endpoint certificates that can be independently checked and used as gold standards for approximate solvers.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a refinement \(G\) and a raw branch \(r\).  Its feasibility set is the basic closed semialgebraic set
\[
S_{G,r}(p)=\left\{\lambda:
\lambda_a(k)\ge0,
\ \sum_{k\in\mathcal K_{G,r,a}}\lambda_a(k)=1\ \text{for every }a,
\ P_G(\lambda)(w)=p(w)\ \text{for every }w
\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
It has at most \(k_G\) scalar variables, at most \(s_G\) polynomial predicates, and degree at most \(D_G\) by the definitions of these compiler parameters.  Clearing the denominator separately in each observed-cell equation turns (10) into an integer system.  Its structural coefficients are integers produced by finite sums of zero--one recursion indicators, while the input rational cells have encoding length at most \(B\); the resulting coefficient bit length is \(O(B)\) up to a factor absorbed by \((s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}\).

Apply \(\text{lem:one-block-real-algebraic-elimination}\) to the existential sentence \(\exists\lambda\, [\lambda\in S_{G,r}(p)]\).  It terminates and decides emptiness.  Retaining the sign-invariant elimination trace gives a replayable certificate whenever (10) is empty; this always satisfies the alternative between a trace and a Positivstellensatz identity in \(\text{def:exact-certifier}\), whether or not an optional rational identity is also extracted.

For a feasible branch, introduce one free variable \(t\) and the additional equation
\[
t-q_G(\lambda)=0.
\tag{11}
\]
One-block elimination of \(\lambda\) computes an exact quantifier-free description of
\[
Q_{G,r}(p)=\{t\in\mathbb R:\exists\lambda\in S_{G,r}(p),\ t=q_G(\lambda)\}.
\tag{12}
\]
The set \(S_{G,r}(p)\) is closed in a product of simplices and hence compact; \(q_G\) is polynomial and therefore continuous.  Thus (12) is nonempty and compact.  Its two boundary extrema occur either at \(-1\) or \(1\), or at a real root of a univariate output polynomial.  Square-free factorization and exact real-root isolation therefore return a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval for each branch extremum.  Applying the sample-point part of the cited elimination result to (10)--(11), with \(t\) fixed by its real-algebraic encoding, returns algebraic coordinates \(\lambda^*\) in the endpoint fiber.

Adding the single variable and equation in (11) changes \(k_G,s_G,D_G\) only by absolute constants.  The cited bounds consequently give, per branch,
\[
B^{O(1)}(s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}
\]
bit operations, endpoint degree \(D_G^{O(k_G)}\), and coefficient bit length \(B(s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}\).  By \(\text{lem:finite-refinements}\), there are exactly
\[
R_{\Sigma}=\sum_{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}|\mathcal R_G|
\]
branches.  Exact comparison of their algebraic extrema by sign determination has the same per-item asymptotic cost.  Summing and using the three maxima gives
\[
R_{\Sigma}B^{O(1)}(s_{\max}D_{\max})^{O(k_{\max})}.
\tag{13}
\]

By \(\text{thm:sharp-refinement-envelope}\), the fiber is empty exactly when every set (10) is empty, so the finite enumeration ledger together with all branch traces is an exact empty-fiber certificate.  In the nonempty case, the least and greatest branch extrema are exactly \(\underline q(p)\) and \(\overline q(p)\).  The reconstruction part of that theorem decodes each algebraic \(\lambda^*\) into independent finite latent weights and deterministic structural tables, yielding an endpoint-attaining SCM.  Finally, directed candidates are computed from \(d,H,L,E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\), bidirected candidates from \(E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow}\) and \(H\), and the finite table enumeration computes every branch parameter.  Hence \(R_{\Sigma},k_{\max},s_{\max},D_{\max}\) are derived inputs rather than hidden oracle quantities, completing all claims.
